request.route_rule: route is exactly one frozen {slot,model,thinking} row and slot equals request.slot
request.provider_input_rule: UTF-8 encoding of provider_input_utf8 must exactly match provider_input_sha256 and provider_input_bytes

synthetic.identity_rule: task_id, thread_id, and turn_id are distinct deterministic hashes of the run/row/nonce/input/attempt binding
synthetic.full_metadata: Every scenario returns the full ordered synthetic poll list, typed terminal status, process return code, task-terminal observation, output digest/count, and reaped state.

sequence: create one fresh thread with requested model and allowProviderModelFallback=false
start one first-attempt turn with provider_input_utf8 as the only text input
wait synchronously in-process until the matching rollout task_complete
reopen and validate exact rollout identity, route, target-turn-scoped sole input, terminal, output, hash, and byte count
actual.identity_limitation: Codex app-server exposes a fresh thread_id and its sole turn_id but no separate platform task_id. task_id is therefore the stable derived value codex-task:<thread_id>, not a separately exposed platform identity; freshness is proven by the new thread plus its one new turn and the request nonce.
actual.rollout_capture: The result binds the exact reopened JSONL path, SHA-256, byte count, row count, session metadata, matching turn context, task_started, task_complete, sole target-turn provider-input message, all raw assistant final messages, and all prohibited response items.

rollout_selector.scope: ordered target turn after its sole matching turn_context, not session-wide user-message cardinality
rollout_selector.precontext_rule: Zero, one, or multiple app/session precontext user response_items before the matching turn_context remain non-provider rollout evidence even when their passthrough turn_id equals the requested turn.
rollout_selector.identity_rule: Exactly one session_meta binds both session_id and id to the fresh thread; exactly one turn_context, task_started, and task_complete exist and each binds to the requested turn, with task_started before turn_context and task_complete after it.
rollout_selector.provider_input_rule: Exactly one user message response_item exists after the matching turn_context across the remaining rollout; it is before task_complete, its internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough.turn_id equals the requested turn, and its sole exact {type:input_text,text} content equals provider_input_utf8 byte-for-byte.
rollout_selector.assistant_final_rule: Exactly one assistant final_answer message exists, is bound by passthrough turn_id to the requested turn, and is ordered after the admitted provider input and before the sole matching task_complete.
rejects: malformed provider-input content that is not exactly one input_text string
any extra post-context or post-terminal user message
provider input associated with another turn
multiple matching or other turn_context rows
missing, duplicate, extra, or wrong-turn task_started/task_complete rows
zero, duplicate, out-of-interval, or wrong-turn assistant finals

actual.output_normalization: One structurally valid raw assistant final output_text is admitted unchanged when it already has a terminal LF, otherwise exactly one LF is appended. Raw final-message evidence and raw-text hashes remain preserved; no trimming, parsing, repair, or duplicate merge occurs.
actual.prohibited_activity_rule: Every response_item outside the explicit message/reasoning safe set is preserved with types and digest. Presence forces a nonzero backend returncode even if app-server itself exits zero.
actual.development_prohibition: Do not invoke actual mode or a provider during development or synthetic self-test.
